info.title: BaseStonk API
info.description: Indexed data for every BaseStonk launch on Base (chain 8453), Robinhood Chain (chain 4663) and Arc (chain 5042); every read takes a `chain`. Open reads, no key. Budgets are cost-weighted per IP: 1,500 cost units per 5 minutes, 1 unit per 100 rows, searches +5. Responses evolve additively - ignore unknown fields. Operations tagged `agents` are the surface meant for agents; the rest is the full HTTP surface the site itself uses. Docs: https://docs.basestonk.io/integration/api

post.description: Three legs, chosen by the PAIR: an oracle-priced pair launches through the current advanced generation, an ecosystem pair through the gate, and a B20 wrapped equity (0xb2000000 prefix, NVDAc and the rest) through the B20 launcher - which carries no vesting, sniper, rewards, max wallet or basket, and refuses them rather than dropping them. `standard: 'b20'` asks for the B20 leg against any registry-priced pair when the live B20 generation takes the token on either side of the pool. Returns an UNSIGNED transaction, the decoded intent it encodes, a verdict of checks run against the chain as it is now, and the block the preparation expires at. The API never signs, relays or broadcasts - sign and send it yourself. Requires a bearer with the `prepare` scope (POST /api/v1/agent/session with {"scopes":["read","prepare"]}, signing the agent:session:prepare action). Answers 422 with the full verdict when a check fails, never 200 with a quiet flag. The idempotency key IS the salt - keccak256(sender, salt), which is what CREATE2 collision-checks on chain - so re-preparing identical inputs yields the same key and the same token address. When the request carries a dev buy, the answer may also carry an approvalTx - send that first and wait for it, because a dev buy makes the launcher pull the pair token and without the allowance the launch reverts inside the token. Both launch legs are prepared: registered pairs through `launch`, ecosystem pairs through `launchGated` with the gate-verified route forwarded verbatim - intent.leg says which.

chainId.description: Which chain to prepare for: 8453 (Base, the default) or 4663 (Robinhood Chain). Absent means Base, so existing callers are unchanged. On 4663 the launch goes through RhLauncher: the pair must be admitted by RhPairRegistry (a Robinhood stock token with supply, USDG, WETH, or a registered feed), marketCapUsd must be $250-$15,000, and there is no gated, direct or B20 leg, no basket issuers and no renounceBasket. A pair whose venue needs a checkpoint answers 409 with a checkpointTx to send first. tx.chainId names the chain the calldata is for.

pairToken.description: The pair token address. The pair decides the leg: one the oracle registry holds a feed for launches through `launch`, and an ecosystem token is priced by a gate-verified route and launches through `launchGated`. intent.leg names which was used. A pair that is neither is refused with the verdict explaining why.

marketCapUsd.description: Opening market cap in dollars. Supply is fixed, so this is the opening price.

metadataUri.description: ipfs:// URI for the token metadata.

creator.description: The creator wallet. Defaults to the bearer's wallet and may only be that wallet.

devBuyPair.description: Dev buy in RAW UNITS OF THE PAIR TOKEN, as an integer string. The response reports the dollar value and the share of supply beside it. Zero (the default) opens the pool single-sided and needs none of the pair token.

vestDays.description: Days the dev buy is locked in a LaunchVesting vault. Zero (the default) sends it to the creator wallet. Non-zero also lifts the dev-buy size cap, because the launcher routes a vested buy to the vault uncapped.

cliffDays.description: Days before any vested tokens unlock. Cannot exceed vestDays.

sniperSeconds.description: Seconds of decaying opening tax that discourages snipers. Zero (the default) opens at the ordinary rate. The opening rate itself is the venue's, not the caller's.

basket.description: The dividend basket - what holders are paid IN. Up to 10 slots of {token, weightBps, issuer?}, weights totalling exactly 10000. Each token must be admitted by the gate. A slot naming the pair token means "leave this share in the pair". Needs the current launcher generation.

standard.description: 'b20' launches a B20 token (Base's native token standard) against any registry-priced pair, not only a B20 one. A B20 pair always launches B20. B20 carries no vesting, sniper, basket, rewards or max wallet.

renounceBasket.description: Freeze the payout basket in the launch transaction. IRREVERSIBLE - the distributor has no function to unset it. Default false.

payees.description: Where the creator's share goes: [{to, shareBps}]. Shares are of the creator's share and must total exactly 100% once burnBps, liquidityBps and rewardsBps are counted. Omitted means the creator takes all of it.

buyTaxBps.description: Buy tax in basis points. Default 100.

sellTaxBps.description: Sell tax in basis points. Defaults to buyTaxBps. Independent rates are a V6 feature.

burnBps.description: Share of the creator's fees burnt. Default 0.

liquidityBps.description: Share of the creator's fees added to liquidity. Default 0.

maxWalletBps.description: Max wallet as basis points of supply. 0 (the default) is no cap.

rewardsBps.description: Share of the creator's fees routed to holders as dividends, counted with burnBps, liquidityBps and payees toward exactly 100%. Default 0. With no payees the creator takes the remainder; 10000 sends all of it to holders.

post.description: Returns an UNSIGNED swap through the venue router, quoted at the TOKEN'S OWN tax - 65 of 459 live tokens are not at 1%, and a flat-rate quote lands under the slippage tolerance and reverts as TooLittleReceived. The API never signs, relays or broadcasts. Requires a bearer with the `prepare` scope. Answers 422 with the full verdict when a check fails. May carry an approvalTx to send first. idempotencyKey is null by design: a swap has no natural key the chain enforces, and two identical swaps are two legitimate trades - a manufactured key would promise a dedupe nothing honours.

chainId.description: Which chain the token lives on: 8453 (Base, the default) or 4663 (Robinhood Chain). Absent means Base. The router, pool manager and quote follow it, and tx.chainId names it.

side.description: "buy" (spend the pair token) or "sell" (spend the launched token).

amountIn.description: RAW UNITS of the input currency as an integer string - the pair token on a buy, the launched token on a sell. The response reports the human amount and USD value beside it.

slippageBps.description: Tolerance below the quote in basis points. Default 300.

post.summary: Exchange a signed EIP-4361 message for a bearer
post.description: Returns the same bearer POST /api/v1/agent/session does. The message must be canonical EIP-4361 for domain basestonk.io, www.basestonk.io, api.basestonk.io with a URI on that domain, a chain id this venue serves, and a nonce from GET /siwe/nonce. Scopes are named in the message resources as urn:basestonk:scope:<scope> - one of read, prepare, upload, token:edit, token:handover - so the wallet shows what it delegates; none named grants read only. upload, token:edit and token:handover let the bearer stand in for the X-Wallet signature on the matching launchpad write. EOA signatures verify locally; smart wallets through ERC-1271 or ERC-6492 on Base.

message.description: The EIP-4361 message exactly as the wallet signed it.

signature.description: The personal_sign signature: 65-byte ECDSA, ERC-1271 or ERC-6492.

scopes.description: Narrow the grant to these. Every one must be named in the message resources; read is always included.

401.description: Wrong domain, chain or URI; a nonce that is forged, expired or used; or a signature that does not match

approvalTx.description: The ERC20 approval a dev buy needs FIRST, or null when none is required. Send this, wait for it, then send tx - a dev buy makes the launcher pull the pair token, and without the allowance the launch reverts inside the token. The amount is exactly the dev buy, never unbounded. A separate field rather than an array because the order is not a detail: fired in parallel on one nonce sequence, the launch races its own precondition.

expiresAtBlock.description: Past this block the preparation is stale - the pair rate moves, the CREATE2 address can be taken, and the simulation was true at one block only.

idempotencyKey.description: On a launch: keccak256(sender, salt) - the on-chain CREATE2 salt itself, not a second key that could disagree with it. On a trade: null by design, because a swap has no natural key the chain enforces and a manufactured one would promise a dedupe nothing honours.

controller.description: Present when a creator edit exists; null while the creator holds the page.

agentBearer.description: A short-lived HMAC bearer from POST /api/v1/agent/session or POST /api/v1/auth/siwe (Sign-In with Ethereum). Reads never need one - an identity only ever unlocks more (a higher budget, keyed to the wallet rather than the IP). The prepare tier requires one carrying the prepare scope; the launchpad uploads and page edits accept one carrying upload, token:edit or token:handover in place of the X-Wallet signature.

agentOAuth.description: The same bearer, issued through OAuth 2.1 for hosts with a sign-in button: PKCE S256, dynamic registration or a client-metadata URL, consent signed by the wallet on basestonk.io. Discovery: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
